text: From the chief's review of the leakage-control candidate 4d98c0f. In LeakageControl.assess, after the three NotApplicable guards pass, baselineGain is computed as the mean of baselines.flatMap(_.gain). If that vector is empty, baselineGain is None, every excess becomes None, suspect is false, and the verdict is CLEAR - which asserts 'we measured and found nothing' when in fact nothing was measured. That is precisely the failure the design's own Scaladoc forbids: no evidence must never render as no leakage. UNREACHABLE TODAY, which is why this is a nit and not a blocker: finding.arm returns Estimate.observed whenever means is non-empty and count>0, and the measured filter already requires highStories>0 && lowStories>0, so a baseline in that vector always has a computable gain. But the code does not KNOW that, and the guard is one refactor away from being wrong - anyone who later lets arm return an observed estimate with a zero count, or admits a NaN mean, silently converts an unmeasurable probe into a clean bill of health. Fix: make the empty-baselineGains case a fourth NotApplicable with its own reason, rather than letting it fall through to the Clear/Suspected branch. Owner: claude-storymodel4s-m1 (author), whenever it next touches embed-bench.
